mods.name: Audio Engine
mods.desc: Engine audio subsystem: IAudioService implementation (Music/SFX/Ambient buses), the auto-advancing music player and the audio factories (music, sounds, playlists). Replaces the former Core/Audio autoloads — the AudioModInitializer adds nodes named AudioService and MusicPlayer to the scene tree root on the boot Scenes phase, so /root/AudioService keeps resolving.

mods.name: CardBattle
mods.desc: Card battle implementation on top of turn_battle_base: an action-card hand with attack/defence values, character cards, battle HUD, log and banners, end-turn flow and its own battle sounds.

mods.name: Characters Engine
mods.desc: Engine characters subsystem: the character and action-card factories (entity kinds 'character' and 'action'), the avatar factory and the character panel UI. Replaces the former Core/Characters factories and Core/UI/CharacterPanel — the CharactersModInitializer publishes kernel contracts (ICharacterTemplateProvider, IActionTemplateProvider, IAvatarProvider) so core code resolves templates without referencing this assembly.

mods.name: Cooking
mods.desc: Autonomous cooking mechanic: the kitchen workbench overlay in home_kitchen with recipe-based cooking (e.g. wolf meat into rations), a ration statistics panel and the home_kitchen_cooking scenario.

mods.name: Cthangover: Story
mods.desc: Story content of the Cthangover game: scenes, scenarios, characters, items, quests, backgrounds and the main game collection.

mods.name: Cthangover: Murakami
mods.desc: Story line about Murakami: a wild wolf prowling the town, the meeting scenario chain (start, wolf battle, werewolf boss, escort home), the Murakami character with her avatar set and the meeting quest.

mods.name: Cthangover: Starter Party
mods.desc: Seeds the default starter party (Marao) and the slave_master skill after mod resources are ready, and restores it on NewGameStartedEvent. Split out of cthangover_game so the base content mod stays pure content (scenes/dialogs/quests/data) with no C# gameplay logic.

mods.name: Dialog Engine
mods.desc: Engine dialog subsystem: DialogBox/DialogCanvas/AnswerBox UI, the dialog queue runtime with the full DSL action set, the .scenario parser with command strategies, the executable event chains and the /root/DialogRunner for interactive dialogs. Replaces the former Core/UI/Dialog, Core/UI/Executable and Core/Scenarios implementations — SceneManager and SaveService keep driving chains and events through the core contracts (IDialogBox, IExecutableEvent, IExecutableEventChain, IScenarioEventFactory).

mods.name: Editor Tools
mods.desc: Developer toolbox of ToolBox windows: scenario graph editor, scene editor (create and change the places of a novel: backgrounds, ambient sound, default scenario, the scene's scenarios), map editor with zones, scene builder with inspector, interactive and light editors, and the mod catalog export window.

mods.name: Effects Engine
mods.desc: Engine effects subsystem: PackedScene visual effect factory (folder mods only) and the frame/animated effect controllers. Replaces the former Core/UI/Animation implementations and Core/Factories/Impls/EffectFactory.

mods.name: FFBattle
mods.desc: Final Fantasy style battle system on top of turn_battle_base: menu-driven commands (attack/defence/item/stun), enemy and party panels, per-action animations and executors, battle HUD and log.

mods.name: Interactive Base
mods.desc: Interactive objects subsystem: JSON-driven scene interactives (hover/click hit areas, highlight effects) with DSL/scenario click actions. Owns InteractiveManager, the interactive definition resolver/factory and the InteractiveEditor data plane.

mods.name: Items Base
mods.desc: Item definitions and factories, inventory and recipe state, inventory UI and their save state

mods.name: Live2D Cubism
mods.desc: Live2D Cubism C# runtime: model loading, rendering, physics, animation, effects

mods.name: Locale Atlas
mods.desc: Localization key map for developers and AI agents: every key declared in locale/*.properties or referenced by scenarios, C#, JSON, scenes, collections and manifests, per language. Reports keys that are missing in some languages, empty, undeclared or duplicated, collection texts without a translation, and the encoding of every locale file (UTF-8 validity, BOM, mojibake, control characters, line endings). Activated by the --locale-atlas user arg; writes report.md/report.json and prints [TEST_RESULT].

mods.name: World Map Engine
mods.desc: Engine world map subsystem: the full-screen map overlay (MapWidget), polygon zones layer, markers, the zone list + runtime override singleton, the scenario-facing map service facade with the open/close/show/hide scenario actions, and the shared zone style and enterability rules. Replaces the former Core/UI/Tool Map* implementations and Core/Actions/MapZoneServiceImpl. The save-format DTO MapZoneStateData stays in the core because RuntimeSerializer owns the __core__ slot layout; the mod plugs into it through MapStateBridge.

mods.name: Menu
mods.desc: Registry-driven main menu: built-in buttons, settings and save/load panels moved out of the core.

mods.name: Mod Manager
mods.desc: Nexus-style mod manager: browse the catalog, filter by category and status, install, update and remove mods.

mods.name: My Novel
mods.desc: The novel template's own content: a town where you can go into a bar or back home, and a way back from both. Only scenes, scenarios and text; backgrounds and sound come from town_pack. Rename it after your game (<game>_game) and grow your story from here.

mods.name: Quests Engine
mods.desc: Engine quests subsystem: the quest factory and runtime state (QuestFactory, QuestBase/QuestData), the IQuestService implementation, quest scenario actions, quest scene conditions with the QuestParser leaf parser and the quest journal UI. Replaces the former Core/Quests state, Core/Actions quest services and actions, Core/Scenes quest conditions and Core/UI/Quests - QuestsModInitializer publishes the kernel contract (IQuestService via QuestServiceRegistry), registers the quest leaf parser and the new-game resettable; QuestsSaveable persists quest state through the generic mod save slot.

mods.name: Recruiting
mods.desc: Recruitment of defeated characters: the roster panel, join conditions (e.g. enslaving a defeated enemy), per-recruit behaviours such as nutrition, the party bridge, tick updates and save state.

mods.name: Resource Atlas
mods.desc: Cross-mod resource map for developers and AI agents: which mod requests resources (sounds, textures, scenes, entities, actions, locale keys, res:// files) provided by another mod, which mod overrides or patches another mod's resources, and whether each link is backed by manifest depends. Activated by the --resource-atlas user arg; writes report.md/report.json and prints [TEST_RESULT].

mods.name: RPG World
mods.desc: Top-down tile world in the spirit of RPG Maker on top of the 2D engine mods: maps of square tiles in three layers (back, main, front) with a collision layer, walking on the grid with WASD or the arrows, events that talk, teleport or start battles with the action key E/F or on touch, random encounters. A map is a logical scene, so entry scenarios, ambience, saving and the dialog box work on maps unchanged; battles run on the turn-based platform with the game's battle core and return to the same cell. Scenario actions: rpg.battle, rpg.teleport.

mods.name: RPG Demo
mods.desc: Content of the RPG demo (collection rpg_demo): a village, the elder's house and a forest with a wolf at the cave, made of rpg_map files over the village_pack tileset. Shows teleports, talking NPCs, events that change with story flags, chests, things to gather in the forest (brushwood, stones, mushrooms that heal), a merchant who sells elixirs and buys the junk, a map monster with a win flag and random encounters in the forest. Only data and scenarios, no C#.

mods.name: RPG Map Editor
mods.desc: Editor of the rpg mod's tile maps (maps/*.json): paints the back, main and front tile layers and the collision layer with a pencil, an eraser and a flood fill from the tileset palette, places and edits map events (look, trigger, scenario, inline commands, teleport, condition), sets the map size, spawn and random encounters. Undo/redo, live update of the running world after saving, play from the spawn. Opens from the main menu tools, the novel editor hub and the in-game toolbar.

mods.name: Scenario Studio
mods.desc: In-game scenario debugger and live editor: a non-modal dock over the running game with pause, step, breakpoints and restarts (with state rollback), the current scenario line, scene candidates with the reason they did or did not start, editable game state, an event log and the scene map. Edits go into folder mods or into a per-game studio layer over read-only mods, which can be exported as a mod; backgrounds dropped into a mod or the layer during the game are picked up with the "Resources" button of the transport bar. Author mode shows the script, novice mode the story moment.

mods.name: 2D Shell
mods.desc: 2D presentation platform: base shell scene with the view box, toolbar, panel slots and notifications. Parent for all 2D mods; content mods fill the shell through scene patches.

mods.name: Skills Engine
mods.desc: Engine skills subsystem: card-based skill definitions, the grant service (skill + granted action pairing), the skills panel UI and the collection effect plate. Replaces the former Core/Skills implementations and Core/Factories/Impls/SkillFactory.

mods.name: Test Defaults and Patches
mods.desc: Test fixture of the property patches system: a targeted patch (Marao, food/ration) and wildcard patches of every character and item. Marked as a fixture, so --all-mods and games never load it; the property_patches itest loads it explicitly (--with-mods=test_defaults_and_patches --itest=property_patches) and checks the merged entities.

mods.name: Time Engine
mods.desc: Engine time subsystem: the in-game clock tick controller bridging SceneEventController timer pulses to RuntimeData.Time, the clock HUD widget, the 2D lighting stack (UiLightController, LampBehaviour, LightDef) installed into the kernel through LightingBridge, and the lighting.clear_map scenario action. Replaces the former Core/Settings/TimeTickController, Core/UI/Lights, Core/UI/Tool/TimeController and Core/Actions/LightingServiceImpl.

mods.name: Town Pack
mods.desc: Reusable town content for any game: the town entrance (with a depth map), a home vestibule, a bar and the bar ambience. Backgrounds: town/town_entry, home/vestibule, bar/bar; sound: bar/bar_ambient.

mods.name: Trading
mods.desc: Shops: merchants defined as data ("Kind": "shop": what they sell, what they buy back and at which price) and a trade window of two inventories side by side, the merchant's goods and the player's bag, with a deal card between them. Money is an ordinary inventory item, the gold coin money/coin by default. Scenario action: trade.open shop=<id>.

mods.name: Turn-based battle engine
mods.desc: Turn-based battle platform: battle ruleset contracts, core registry, action executors, status effects, battle scene, victory/defeat screens, EXP and loot reports

mods.name: UI
mods.desc: Engine UI subsystem: widget toolkit (Widget/ModWidget/lists), ViewBox background viewport, ToolBox toolbar, GameMenu/SaveIcon, notification panels, UiKit design system, DeviceInput. Kernel keeps only contracts (IWidget, IDialogBox, IToolbarHost, ISaveIconHost, IBackgroundView, IUiLazyConstruct, MenuRegistry, ToolFactory, NotificationBuffer, SceneEventController, CthangoverTheme/UiTokens boot styling) and drives this mod through those seams.

mods.name: Validator
mods.desc: Static validation of mods without running the game: manifest schema, entity strategies (characters, items, quests, skills, recipes, actions), cross references, depends, scenario commands and scene patches, with an optional text report.

mods.name: Village Pack
mods.desc: Reusable pixel-art content for RPG maps: the 'village' tileset (grass, paths, water, trees with crowns for the front layer, houses, fences, chests, a forest floor and a cave mouth, things lying on the ground to pick up — brushwood, stones, a mushroom — with solid flags), charsets of a hero, an elder, a villager, a merchant, a slime and a wolf, battle portraits of the hero, the slime and the wolf, and two battle backgrounds (meadow, forest) with depth maps. Art only: no maps, no stories.
